## Choose the tool for the design intent

[Blender](https://www.blender.org/) is excellent for artistic 3D work: mesh editing, organic or sculptural forms, characters, materials, lighting, rendering and animation. Its vertices, edges and faces make it natural to push, pull and sculpt visible form.

Blender can produce printable meshes, but it is not the default teaching tool for dimension-driven fabrication parts. For a bracket, sized hole, repeated pattern or part that must update predictably when one dimension changes, use [Onshape and parametric/solid CAD](../04-3d-printing/01-additive-cad.qmd).

## Focused advanced task

Create a simple original 3D identity object or scene. Build the silhouette from a small number of forms, organize objects and names, set a camera, use intentional light and material choices, and render a still or short turntable. If a logo is imported, inspect and simplify its paths before extruding it.

## Mesh checks

- use transformations deliberately and apply scale when the workflow requires it;
- inspect normals, intersections, holes and extremely thin regions;
- keep source files editable and name important objects;
- use only original or appropriately licensed textures, models and reference images;
- distinguish a visual render from evidence that geometry is manufacturable.
